headline: External references and complementary modalities are being fused to improve cancer prediction and clone assignment
label: Cross Modal Cancer Prediction
summary: Ten new items integrate methylation atlases, bulk-derived cell profiles, evolutionary features and histopathology to strengthen cancer prediction under sparse or incomplete data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is supplementing a limited primary measurement with an external reference or a second modality. mFrag weights cfDNA fragmentomics using methylation atlases, DeSCENT derives reference-informed cellular profiles from bulk RNA-seq for TCGA survival prediction, and EvoSurv adds a 38-dimensional evolutionary representation to clinical and RNA data. OmniT2I converts molecular tables to images and fuses them with histopathology embeddings, predicting missing modalities. KLONE assigns unpaired scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq copy-number clones, and SigBridgeR benchmarks eight algorithms linking bulk phenotypes to single-cell subpopulations. A 1.3M-slide H&E analysis showing recoverable sex, age and race signal is a caution about confounding in foundation-model features. Cell-typing ensembles (scBoost, scDNM) and CellSavior are peripheral to this thread.
